ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a four-variable Karnaugh map, the column variables are labeled PQ, and the column order is 00, 01, 11, 10; the row variables are labeled RS, and the row order is 00, 01, 11, 10. The cell values in each row are: the RS=00 row is 0, 1, 1, 0; the RS=01 row is all 1; the RS=11 row is all 1; the RS=10 row is all 0. Then reason: first combine the 8 ones in the two whole rows RS=01 and RS=11 into one group. In this group, P, Q, and R all change, only S is always 1, so the term S is obtained. The remaining uncovered 1s are located in the RS=00 row and the two columns PQ=01 and PQ=11; combine them with the corresponding two 1s directly below in the RS=01 row to form a 2×2 group. In this group, Q is always 1, R is always 0, while P and S change, so the term Q\bar{R} is obtained. Adding the two terms, the output expression is Q\bar{R}+S.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a 4-variable Karnaugh map with PQ across the columns and RS down the rows. Form one 8-cell group covering the two complete rows RS=01 and RS=11; since only S remains constant at 1, this contributes S. Then cover the remaining uncovered 1s in row RS=00 at columns PQ=01 and PQ=11 by grouping them with the adjacent 1s directly below in row RS=01, forming a 2-by-2 block. In that block Q is always 1 and R is always 0, while P and S vary, so the term is Q\bar{R}. Combine the terms to obtain Q\bar{R}+S.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the 4-variable K-map labels from the image: columns are PQ in Gray order 00, 01, 11, 10 and rows are RS in Gray order 00, 01, 11, 10. planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know that the requested result is the output Boolean expression for the K-map shown; no additional textual data are needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard K-map simplification: group adjacent 1s in powers of two, allow overlapping groups, and for each group keep only variables that remain constant across the group. A full two-row group over RS=01 and RS=11 keeps S=1, giving term S. A 2-by-2 group over rows RS=00 and 01 and columns PQ=01 and 11 keeps Q=1 and R=0, giving Q\bar{R}. OR the group terms.
